The *Nanda Sutta* (Ud 3.2, PTS Ud 21) is a canonical discourse in the *Udāna* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In this narrative, the Buddha intervenes when his half-brother Nanda experiences dissatisfaction with the monastic life; the Buddha makes a pact with him, guaranteeing that if he perseveres as a monk, he will be rewarded with celestial nymphs in his next life. The text is also explicitly referenced in later Pali literature in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.3, *Vatthaguyhanidassanapañha*).
